angularDiameterSource: Limb-darkened angular diameter 0.342 +/- 0.008 mas from the CHARA Array in the K band, Baines et al. (2012, ApJ 761, 57; arXiv:1210.0556), abstract; at the Gaia DR3 distance it is the radius of the astronomy record, 1,045,756 km.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 source 2832463659640297472 (Gaia Collaboration 2023, A&A 674, A1): parallax 24.461952 +/- 0.045453 mas, inverted to 40.8798 pc. Zurlo et al. (2022) fit at 24.525662 mas, so the orbits below keep their angular size and are placed at this distance.
radiusSource: Radius: the CHARA Array limb-darkened angular diameter 0.342 +/- 0.008 mas of Baines et al. (2012, ApJ 761, 57; arXiv:1210.0556) at the Gaia DR3 distance 40.8798 pc: 1,045,756 km, 1.5032 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius (Baines et al. give 1.44 +/- 0.06 solar radii from the same diameter at the Hipparcos parallax of their time). GM from the stellar mass 1.47 solar masses that Zurlo et al. (2022, A&A 666, A133) adopt for the four-planet fit these orbits come from, times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2; Baines et al. derive 1.516 +0.038/-0.024 solar masses from the same diameter. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; the star's spin axis has no measured direction on the sky (Wright et al. 2011 constrain only its inclination, from asteroseismology).
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2012, ApJ 761, 57; arXiv:1210.0556): effective temperature 7193 +/- 87 K from the CHARA limb-darkened diameter and bolometric flux, https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.0556
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 8799 (pscomppars): spectral type A5, from Gravity Collaboration et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623L..11G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 8799 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.5 dex, from Gravity Collaboration et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623L..11G/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 8799 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.73347, from Konopacky et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016AJ....152...28K/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 8799 (pscomppars): age 0.03 Gyr, from Gravity Collaboration et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623L..11G/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 8799 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 34.79 km/s, from Swastik et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161..114S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; the photosphere of a giant star is not a solid surface and its limb is not sharp.
